name: Town of Yorktown
gaps: No height in stories, impervious-coverage or one-family floor-area limits in Appendix A
RSP-1 and RSP-3 property-line yards are not in the schedule (RSP-1 has street setbacks only; RSP-3 is 150 ft from residential zones); RSP-3 is a geriatric-care district (no houses)
Yorktown has no stand-alone steep slope law; slopes are handled through the Ch. 248 erosion-control permit
Split-zoned county codes (with '*') follow each part's rules

wetlands.summary: Ch. 178 Freshwater Wetlands: wetland/watercourse buffer at least 100 ft from the wetland edge, and all land within 100 ft of a watercourse bank or high-water mark, regulated like the wetland; permit needed for structures, filling, excavation, and cutting more than 3 trees over 8 in. per acre per year in wetlands/buffers (§ 178-6 definitions, § 178-9 regulated activities).

steep_slopes.summary: No separate steep-slope permit law. Ch. 248 erosion and sediment control permit covers disturbance of 5,000 sf+ or 50 cu yd+; work on slopes over 25% may be referred to the County Soil and Water Conservation District.

trees.summary: Ch. 270 § 270-6: tree removal permit for 10+ protected trees (8 in.+ DBH) in a year over 10,000 sf, more than 2 protected trees a year in the regulated buffer zone (5 ft from side/rear lines on lots of 1 acre or less), any specimen tree (24 in.+ DBH), land conversion, or disturbing 10,000 sf+ (or 6%) of protected woodland.

stormwater.summary: Ch. 248: stormwater/erosion permit for construction disturbing 5,000 sf or more or moving 50 cu yd+ of soil (Town Engineer administrative permit; Town Board over 20,000 sf or 200 cu yd of fill); SWPPP required for land development activities.

adu.summary: § 300-38: one accessory apartment by ZBA special permit in R1 districts; owner-occupied; 400-1,000 sf and max 40% of the house's usable floor area; max 2 bedrooms; 800 sf max in an existing detached accessory building on lots 40,000 sf+; 3-year renewable permit (§ 300-38 as amended by L.L. 9-2025).

general.accessory_structures: Attached accessory buildings follow main-building rules; detached ones up to 1 story/15 ft may use the schedule's accessory setbacks (10 ft side/rear in R1 and R-2) if behind the front setback line; 20 ft where the accessory footprint is 50%+ of the house in R1-40/R1-20/R1-10/R-2; total accessory footprint max 80% of the house there (§ 300-14; Appendix A note 4).
general.pools: Private pools are accessory uses and must be fully enclosed by a 4 ft protective fence (§ 300-21C(1)(c)[4]); no separate pool setback found.
general.notes: Corner lots need a side yard on the side street equal to the required front yard (§ 300-13G). Front yards add 25 ft (measured from road center line) on streets with under 50 ft right-of-way.

accessory.notes: Detached accessory buildings up to 1 story/15 ft, behind the front setback line, in the rear yard (Appendix A; § 300-14B). Open decks use accessory setbacks (§ 300-13O).

R1-200.source: § 300-21 / Appendix A Residence Zone Standards (300 Attachment 1, Supp 92 May 2026); § 300-13G (corner lots); § 300-14 (accessory buildings)
R1-200.notes: Lot width measured at the main building line. Front setback +25 ft (measured from road center line) on streets with less than a 50 ft right-of-way. Min house size 1,200 sf.

R-3.name: Multi-Family Residential

max_floor_area.text: Usable FAR (public sewers): 0.20 at max 12 units/acre, 0.215 at max 10 u/ac, 0.23 at max 9 u/ac; half without public sewers; on net area excluding wetlands and controlled areas

accessory.notes: Accessory building in rear yard: 20 ft min either side

R-3.source: § 300-21 / Appendix A Residence Zone Standards (300 Attachment 1, Supp 92 May 2026); § 300-13G (corner lots); § 300-14 (accessory buildings)
R-3.notes: 3,630 sf of lot area per unit (12 units/acre), net of wetlands. Multifamily by site plan; buildings 90 ft apart main wall to main wall, max 180 ft long (§ 300-21C(3)). Two-family dwellings also permitted.

RSP-1.name: Age-Oriented Community

max_floor_area.note: Usable FAR with public sewers (Appendix A); half without sewers

RSP-1.source: Appendix A (300 Attachment 1, Supp 92 May 2026); Article XIII § 300-126 (15-acre site), § 300-127 (height, coverage, street setbacks)
RSP-1.notes: Plan of development approved by the Planning Board; max 12 units/acre. Buildings set back 50 ft from main/collector streets and 40 ft from local streets (§ 300-127F); no property-line yards in the schedule.

RSP-2.name: Senior Citizens District

max_floor_area.note: Usable FAR with public sewers; net area

accessory.notes: Rear yard is 'same as side yards'

RSP-2.source: § 300-21 / Appendix A Residence Zone Standards (300 Attachment 1, Supp 92 May 2026); § 300-13G (corner lots); § 300-14 (accessory buildings); Article XIV § 300-152
RSP-2.notes: 5-acre minimum site; 2,200 sf of lot area per unit up to 2 bedrooms, 10,000 sf for larger units. Planning Board special permit; within 1,500 ft of hamlet commercial land. Main-building height may rise to 55 ft on sites over 25 acres (Appendix A note 11, L.L. 7-2025).

RSP-3.name: Age-Oriented Geriatric Community
RSP-3.source: Article XVI § 300-161 Lot and bulk standards
RSP-3.notes: Geriatric center / care facilities only; 25 acres for a combination of facilities; buildings set back 150 ft from lines abutting residential zones; 'maximum of three floors' per § 300-161 intent; 42 ft height applies where a nursing home is part of a geriatric center.
